Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the chat this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a short mutual action plan (attached) that maps who owns each milestone for your Dedicated GPU pool provisioning. Key items we need to lock down before we schedule provisioning:

- Preferred region(s) for primary capacity (US-West vs US-East)
- Target baseline throughput (r/s and avg tokens/s) for production traffic
- Burst policy limits (max concurrent sessions and burst duration)
- KV/prefix caching expectations (percent of inference calls that can use warm cache)
- Procurement windows for dedicated contract and any compliance paperwork (SOC 2 evidence)

I attached a draft MPA and a capacity diagram. If you can confirm the region and an initial RPS/throughput estimate by EOD Wednesday, we can book a Dedicated activation slot for the week of July 26 and reserve the bursted burst buffer.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_mpa_v1.xlsx, capacity_schema_diagram.png

Thanks —

Marcus —

Thanks for the MPA, looks good at a high level. A few clarifying items from our side before we commit: 

1) Region: we prefer primary in us-east-1 for latency to our east coast tenants, but would like automatic failover to us-west-2.

2) Throughput: initial pilot will see ~25 r/s with spikes up to 110 r/s during batch runs. Steady-state after Q4 expected ~80 r/s.

3) Burst behaviour: we need a short 10-minute burst window that can scale to +4x baseline for safety (we're particularly concerned about sudden spikes from report generation jobs).

4) Security: procurement asked for SOC 2 evidence and retention policy documentation — attaching procurement contact.

I can confirm region + rough throughput by tomorrow. Also looping in procurement for contract timelines.

—Laura

Forwarding Laura's note — she confirmed region preference (us-east primary, us-west secondary) and gave spike numbers. High level ask from CS/procurement: 10-minute bursts to 4x baseline and SOC 2 artifacts.

Questions for infra and product:
- Can we guarantee automatic failover cross-region within our Dedicated offering without customer-visible token loss? Any known constraints for prefix cache warm-up during failover?
- For a 10-minute burst to 4x, what sizing recommendation do we put in the MPA (pool size, buffer capacity, and recommended autoscale policy parameters)?

I attached the MPA for reference. If we can get a recommended config today, I'll send back to Laura with a proposed activation date.

Marcus

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity provisioning: mutual action plan & autoscale constraints

Marcus / team —

Quick runbook notes from infra/ops perspective:

1) Cross-region failover: we support active-primary with automatic fallback to secondary; however, cache (KV/prefix) is local to the pool. Failover will cause cache misses until the KV is re-populated — recommend a staged warm-up: pre-warm top 20% of hot prefixes via synthetic traffic during cutover window. We can automate pre-warm during the activation job.

2) Sizing for 4x 10-minute burst: baseline 25 r/s -> peak 100 r/s. For safety (and expected Q4 growth), plan initial pool to handle 120 r/s sustained for 15 minutes. Recommended GPU pool: 8x A100-equivalent instances with continuous batching enabled and a burst buffer of 4 extra nodes that autoscale-in at T+12min.

3) Autoscale policy template:
- scale-out threshold: CPU/Infer slots > 70% for 30s
- max concurrent sessions per pool: 700
- burst limit: additional 50% capacity for up to 10 minutes
- cooldown: 8 minutes

4) Compliance: SOC 2 artifacts — point Monica to the evidence bundle link. Procurement will need signed data processing addendum (DPA) before go-live.

I'll prepare an action snippet for the MPA and a short activation checklist (provision, pre-warm, smoke tests, canary traffic, failover test). If no objections, I'll push numbers into the MPA and share to Laura.

-Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity provisioning: mutual action plan & autoscale constraints

Laura / team —

Thanks for the confirmation earlier in the week. Per Rishi's sizing notes (below) we've updated the mutual action plan and proposed an activation timetable:

- Primary region: us-east-1, failover target: us-west-2
- Initial pool: 8 A100-equivalent nodes + 4-node burst buffer (autoscale-in at T+12m)
- Autoscale template: scale-out at >70% slot utilization (30s), burst cap = +50% capacity for 10 minutes, cooldown 8 minutes
- Pre-warm: automated pre-warm of top-20% prefixes during the activation window (we'll coordinate the synthetic traffic window)
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence bundle and DPA link (attached). Procurement — if you can sign the DPA and confirm contract start date by end of week, we can schedule provisioning for July 28.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_mpa_v1.xlsx, soc2-evidence-request.pdf

Next steps (action owners):
- Atlas: confirm procurement signature + contract start date (Procurement)
- Redwood Ops: provision pool and run pre-warm (Rishi)
- CS/Implementation: schedule activation call and canary test (Marissa)

Please reply with any blockers. If not, we'll lock July 28 as the activation run.

Best —
